PUBLIC COMMENTS:

Michael Silber, Westlake Village, business owner of Da Bobblehead, with daughters

groups. Mr. Silber responded to Council questions regarding market share and purchase

STAFF COMMENTS:

City Manager de Geus provided an update on the drought conditions and stated that the
Las Virgenes Municipal Water District (LVMWD) Board adopted one-day-per-week
watering restrictions effective June 1, 2022. He noted that the majority of the City's parks
and medians use recycled water and are under a different set of restrictions. Mr. de Geus
reported that the City is in close contact and in partnership with LVMWD, and that
Administrative Analyst Mott is a member of the newly formed group, City Outreach
Partnership for Conservation & Drought, led by the Water District. He said this group meets
weekly and develops various outreach messages.

City Manager de Geus stated City is working with LVMWD on other opportunities such as
the expansion of the Emergency Recycled Water Distribution Program, the City's website
"Water" page is updated weekly, and that the City drafted a letter to Westlake Village
Homeowner's Associations (HOA) regarding the drought and related restrictions. A joint
HOA Presidents and City Council meeting will be held on June 22, 2022, 4:00 pm, at City
Hall and the drought topic will be discussed. Questions related to the drought are addressed
on the Water District's website, www.lvmwd.com . Deputy City Manager Eskandar
presented graphs from the Metropolitan Water District depicting water levels at Lake
Oroville Reservoir Storage and Northern Sierra Snowpack levels and explained the current
trends. Mr. Eskandar noted that further information can be found at www.mwdh20.com.
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  May 25. 2022  3

  COUNCIL COMMENTS:

  Councilmember Pearl commented on Mayor Halpern's opening of tonight's meeting
  offering words of empathy and a moment of silence. Mr. Pearl read a Facebook message
  from a Three Springs resident regarding the mass shooting in Uvalde, Texas yesterday.

  Councilmember Mcsweeney reiterated Mayor Halpern's words, "Stand and be heard", and
  asked for everyone to stand.

  Councilmember Davis commented on the Las Virgenes Unified School District's approach
  creating school culture and having zero tolerance for bullying. Mr. Davis asked the
  community to be cognizant of how we treat each other and what it means to be a
  community.

  MONTHLY DEPARTMENTAL REPORTS:

  1.  Sheriff's Department Report

  Deputy Brian Knott presented the Sheriff Department's report for the month of April
  2022 including crime statistics and noting that crime is down from a year ago.
  City Manager de Geus introduced Captain Jennifer Seetoo who was recently
  promoted to Captain of the Lost Hills Sheriff's Station. Captain Seetoo expressed
  appreciation to the Council for acknowledging the Texas shooting incident. She
  provided a brief synopsis of her background and stated that her three main topics of
  focus were suppressing crime, disaster preparedness, and traffic incidents. Captain
  Seetoo is looking forward to working in collaboration with cities within the community.
  2.  Fire Department Report

  Assistant Fire Chief Drew Smith presented the Fire Department's report for the
  month of April 2022 on the number of fires, medical response calls, and rescue
  activities conducted. Chief Smith commented on the working relationship with the
  Sheriff's Department complimenting the public safety endeavor.

  Chief Smith responded to Councilmember Mcsweeney regarding what residents
  can do about the drought situation and explained the balance between ember-
  receptiveness and dryness of ornamental vegetation.
  3.  Chamber of Commerce Report

  Adam Haverstock, Director of Government Affairs and Tourism, highlighted recent
  and upcoming events of the Greater Conejo Chamber of Commerce including the

J  2022 Recognition Gala held on May 20, 2022 honoring individuals and businesses
  throughout the community, Chamber is seeking nominations for their Forty Under
  Forty Awards program, and members of the Chamber's Board will be traveling to
  Sacramento to accept an award from tile California Chamber of Commerce 13th
  Annual Cal Chamber President's Circle Award for excellence in government affairs
  and helping businesses stay compliant with changing Human Resource laws.

2.  Planning Department Report

  Planning Director Forbes provided the Planning Department's Status Report stating
  that a virtual community workshop to discuss the upcoming transition to Zero-
  emissions Landscape Equipment is scheduled for Thursday, May 26, 2022 at 6:30
  p.m. and noted that additional information is available on the City's website
  www.wlv.org . Mr. Forbes mentioned that the presentation will be geared mainly
  toward homeowners and noted that the City will be conducting a series of meetings
  for homeowners and a series of meetings geared toward gardeners and landscape
  professionals. Responding to Council questions, Mr. Forbes said the meeting will be
  recorded and available for viewing.

3.  Cultural Recreation Report

  Deputy City Manager Philippe Eskandar presented the Cultural Recreation
  Department's Status Report and highlighted upcoming events of the City's Summer
  Entertainment Series including Saturday Concerts in the Park, a Movie Night, TGIF
  events at the Civic Center, and 4th of July events. Mr. Eskandar stated that summer
  programs commence on Friday, May 27, 2022, at 7:00 p.m. with a TGIF concert at
  the Civic Center Courtyard featuring performances by the Lindero Canyon Middle
  School and Agoura High School Jazz bands. He noted that food trucks would be
  available starting at 6:00 p.m.

  1.  APPROVAL OF A PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH STANLEY
  R. HOFFMAN ASSOCIATES TO PREPARE A DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEE
  STUDY AND A SPECIAL BENEFIT ASSESSMENT DISTRICT STUDY FOR THE
  NORTH BUSINESS PARK SPECIFIC PLAN AREA

J  City Manager de Geus introduced the item for consideration of an agreement with
  Stanley R. Hoffman Associates to conduct the analysis necessary to establish
  development impact fees and a special benefit assessment district in the North
  Business Park Specific Plan (NBPSP) area.

  Senior Planner Sinkula provided an amended copy of Old Business 1, Attachment
  1 at the meeting and explained the changes.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  May 25, 2022  6

OLD BUSINESS (continued) :

  Providing background, Senior Planner Sinkula reported that in June 2020 the City
  Council adopted the NBPSP to establish a vision and development framework to
  guide reinvestment in the specific plan area including recommendations of pursuing
  a variety of strategies to implement the plan and identifying various cost recovery
  and funding opportunities. In January 2021 Stanley R. Hoffman Associates prepared
  memos discussing three funding opportunities for cost recovery and capital
  improvements including  Cost recovery fees,  Development impact fees, and
  Special benefit assessment district.

  On February 23, 2022, the City Council conducted a public hearing and adopted
  specific plan cost recovery fees. Ms. Sinkula addressed the remaining two funding
  opportunities.

  Special Benefit Assessment District

  Senior Planner Sinkula explained that the Special Benefit Assessment District is:

  1. Created by local government to fund capital improvements and maintenance
  within a defined district area.
  2. Bonds are issued to raise funds upfront for infrastructure improvements.
  3. Bond payments are passed through to property owners in the district to
  reimburse the City over time.

  Ms. Sinkula noted that the City currently has Assessment Districts for landscape and
  lighting in residential areas and that if an Assessment District was established for
  the Specific Plan area, it would likely be for streetscape improvements such as
  landscaping and street trees, signs and street furniture, and pedestrian and transit
  enhancements. She mentioned that property owners would be assessed based on
  their proportional share of benefit from the improvements to the district and provided
  estimated annual assessment costs for capital improvements and maintenance.

  Reviewing the process, Ms. Sinkula explained that:

  a. All property owners in the district can vote to support or oppose the formation
  of the district,
  b. Votes are weighted by proportionate financial obligation of each property -
  one vote per dollar to be assessed per property,
  c. Simple majority of weighted votes are required to establish a district, and
  d. Once established, the District is administered by the City.

  The Land Use Committee (Pearl/Honig) reviewed the proposed fees and underlying
  methodology and assumptions on January 27, 2022, and May 4, 2022, and
  expressed concerns for the level of support that would likely be seen by property
  owners in the NBPSP area for the creation of the Assessment District. Ms. Sinkula
   City Council Minutes
  City of Westlake Village  May 25, 2022  7

  OLD BUSINESS (continued) :

  stated that staff recommended a phased approach for this effort to gauge the level
  of support without expending the full budget of this item.

l  Phase One - $8,600 for the development and implementation of a property owner
  survey to gauge support for the creation of the Assessment District and to obtain
  input from property owners as to what types of capital improvements would be most
  beneficial to their individual properties. Subsequent phases would proceed based
  on outcome of Phase One and Land Use Committee direction.

  Phase Two - $24,200 - Pending outcome of Phase One, update analysis prepared
  in January 2021 to reflect current construction costs and planned improvements and
  to refine methodology used and use the analysis to estimate assessments on
  parcels that would receive benefits from capital improvements.

  Development Impact Fees

  Senior Planner Sinkula explained that Development Impact Fees are intended to
  cover the costs of capital improvements noting that improvements need not be within
  a defined district area and cannot be used for operations and maintenance. Ms.
  Sinkula stated that potential new fees would be used for capital improvements to
  parks, library, City facilities, and drainage facilities. She explained that Development
  Impact Fees are:

  1) Imposed only on new development, typically when a building permit is issued,
  2) A one-time payment, not an annual assessment, and
  3) Can only be used to fund capital needs arising from the impact of new
  development.

  Ms. Sinkula stated the agreement would authorize Stanley R. Hoffman Associates
  to conduct the analysis necessary to establish Development Impact Fees, at a cost
  of $34,800, including:

  1.Developing growth projections for residential and non-residential development
  in the Specific Plan area.
  2. Establishing current and projected capital needs.
  3. Converting capital needs to estimated capital costs.
  4. Establishing a fair share allocation of the capital costs to new development.

J  The Land Use Committee recommended bringing these options to the full City
  Council for consideration. The Committee noted that any fees are a potential
  constraint to development and the City should consider that when contemplating
  new fees. They also expressed concern that establishment of an Assessment
  District may not be supported by property owners in the NBPSP area, and 3.
  Recommended use of the phased approach for the Assessment District to gauge
  property owner support before commencing with the full study.
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  May 25, 2022  8

OLD BUSINESS (continued) :

  Following City Council discussion, it was the consensus that information and
  collaboration received from businesses by conducting the Phase One survey would
  be beneficial to the City and the outcome will determine proceeding with Phase Two.

  Councilmember Mcsweeney moved that the City Council approve a Professional
  Services Agreement with Stanley R. Hoffman Associates for preparation of a
  development impact fee study and special benefit assessment district survey and
  study and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement. Councilmember
  Honig seconded the motion.

  YES:  Councilmembers Mcsweeney, Honig, Davis, Mayor Pro Tern
  Pearl, and Mayor Halpern
  NO:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN :  None

NEW BUSINESS:

1.  MALIBU FOUNDATION CLIMATE VULNERABILITY DISCUSSION

  City Manager de Geus introduced Shea Cunningham and Dean Kubani from The
  Malibu Foundation who presented an overview of their recently completed
  Resilience Report.

  Ms. Cunningham reported the project's three objectives included: ldentifing climate
  change hazards in the region with a focus on most vulnerable populations;,
  Proposing strategies to increase climate resilience, sustainability, and capacity to
  adapt to extreme heat, fire and other hazards, and Serving as an actionable guide
  for regional collaboration by local governments, regional agencies, individuals,
  neighborhood groups and other stakeholders.

  Ms. Cunningham and  Mr.  Kubani  provided  comprehensive findings  and
  recommendations on:

  a.  Methodology
  b.  Climate Hazard Assessment
  c.  Wildfire Risk to Potential Structures
  d.  Extreme Precipitation Comparison
  e.  Road Vulnerability
  f.  Coastal Flooding Hazard Sea Level Rise & 100-Year Storm
  g.  Social Vulnerabilities
  h.  Critical Infrastructure Assessment
   City Council Minutes
City of Westlake Village  May 25. 2022  9

NEW BUSINESS (continued):

  Mr. Kubani explained Malibu Foundation's next steps, 2022 commitments and
  provided links to the Executive Summary www.thema libufoundation.org/executive-
  summary,  Our  Climate  Crisis  Full  Report
  www.themalibufoundation.org/resilience-report.
